messages:
Ava (Design): Pushing a quick Figma update — main ask: opinions on adding a 'smoothing' toggle AND a separate 'outlier handling' mode in the chart toolbar. figma: https://figma.com/file/xxxxx (mock)
Ravi (Frontend): Quick look — my instinct: default smoothing off for raw metrics, but enable an opt-in smoothing toggle. saves time for debugging. :thumbsup:
Morgan (Product): Agree on default off. Also we need copy that makes intent clear for non-technical PMs. 'Smooth series (hide short-term noise)' maybe?
Kai (Accessibility): If we add toggles, they must be keyboard-focusable and have accessible labels. e.g., aria-pressed & aria-describedby linking to help text.
Liam (Eng): Performance note: client-side smoothing on large series can be heavy. Could we do server-side downsample + smoothing when requested? Or a light-weight algorithm in the renderer.
Ava (Design): Good point about copy. Alternative text: 'Apply smoothing to reduce spike noise — preserves trend'. Also thinking of an icon-only toggle vs labeled. accessibility prefers visible label.
Ravi (Frontend): Icon-only becomes ambiguous. I'd prefer a short label plus tooltip. Tooltip should appear on hover/focus. For the toggle we can expose props: <Chart smoothingToggle label="Smoothing" />
Ravi (Frontend): Example quick prop sketch:
```
<Chart
  data={...}
  smoothing={{enabled: false, window: 5}}
  outlierMode="clip" // clip | show | mark
/>
```
Morgan (Product): Outlier modes — we talked about 3: show raw, clip top/bottom percentiles, and mark as dots with a tooltip. Which should be default?
Ava (Design): I think default should be 'show raw' to avoid surprising folks. But display a subtle legend badge: 'Density spikes: try smoothing or clipping' with a CTA to toggle.
Kai (Accessibility): If we add a legend badge CTA, ensure it's reachable via keyboard and reads as a button. Also the badge should not rely solely on color to communicate status.
Liam (Eng): For clip mode we need to define algorithm: clip at a percentile (e.g., 99th) or use IQR. IQR is robust and explainable. Implementation note: we can compute IQR client-side cheaply.
Ravi (Frontend): Minor ticks & axis label spacing — small UX nit: when smoothing is on, maybe we reduce minor tick density to avoid clutter. Also unit rendering — support compact units (k, M) but accessible full-value on hover.
Ava (Design): Copy tweak for axis unit: 'Units (auto): token / sec' rather than 'auto (tokens)'. Keep it short.
Morgan (Product): +1 on full-value reveal on hover. Also add a keyboard shortcut to toggle smoothing? maybe `s` when chart focused.
Kai (Accessibility): If adding 's' shortcut, must announce via aria-live when toggled and ensure no conflict with other app shortcuts. Also add a way to turn off shortcuts.
Ravi (Frontend): Tooltip content example for outlier dots: "Value: 12,345 (99th percentile) — hover to expand". For screen readers, expose a longdesc or aria-describedby that reads full value and mode.
Liam (Eng): Edge case: streaming charts with smoothing enabled — we must maintain KV cache for incoming points to keep window consistent. Implementation complexity note.
Ava (Design): Design ask: add a small legend control area with: [Smoothing toggle] [Outlier dropdown] [Units select]. Make sure toolbar wraps responsively on narrow screens.
Ravi (Frontend): I can prototype responsive wrap with flex-gap and a dropdown collapse into an overflow menu for mobile.
Morgan (Product): Let's decide defaults for the next release: smoothing off, outlier mode show raw, units auto. Add a small help icon linking to docs.
Kai (Accessibility): Final checklist from me: 1) All toggles keyboard-focusable 2) ARIA labels + aria-describedby for tooltips 3) Live region for shortcuts 4) Color contrast for badges >= 4.5
Ava (Design): Thanks — I'll update mock with labelled toggle, legend badge, and a11y notes. Will ping when updated. :eyes:
